pairs.subject: roll-call-vote-analysis
pairs.evidence: lib/analysis/kg.ts:189 rebellion() and partyCohesion() take one club per mandate for the whole term rather than the club on the day of the division, and clubAt.ts (same context, lines 4-6) itself records that this repaints a club-switcher's historical ballots with the wrong club line.

techniques.evidence: lib/analysis/kg.ts:189 Strict majority with ties skipped (l.222-223) and the MIN_ELIGIBLE_VOTES floor are correct. But membership is static per mandate, not resolved at division time. The stat is keyed by person with the first club seen (l.200-204). Mandates with no club are dropped silently with no count (l.190). The ranking sort (l.239) goes rate then person id, with no absolute-rebellion-count tiebreak.

lib/analysis/kg.ts:140 Pairs below MIN_SHARED_VOTES are pruned at write time, and no discarded-pair count ships with the output. The doc comment (l.82-83) says pruning is left to the reader, which contradicts the code. Nothing enforces one resolved ballot per person per division, so a person with two mandates on the same vote adds two entries. Positional-only sharing, voided exclusion, the canonical src<dst cell and dense typed arrays are all correct.

lib/analysis/kg.ts:289 Positional base only, voided votes excluded, per-vote floor MIN_CLUB_POSITIONAL is a named constant (l.288). A club with no qualifying votes is left out of the map (not measured, never 0). The qualifying-vote count ships with the mean. It also inherits the static club mapping.

lib/analysis/volby/contested.ts:30 kg.ts:49 imports POSITIONAL_CHOICES correctly. But listLine() in contested.ts re-lists its qualifying choices inline over an untyped string choice, which forks the one exported positional set.

lib/analysis/kg.ts:29 Consumes the single VoteChoice vocabulary and its sets from the normalize package. That package has an explicit unknown, the merged abstain_or_not_voting value and sentinel detection. It is not restated here.

pairs.subject: roll-call-vote-analysis
pairs.evidence: features/volby/getListData.ts:52 Each contested vote gets a party-list line built from whatever member ballots exist, with no line-support floor. A list with no positional ballots on that vote shows the same 'split' as a real tie. ContestedMatrix shows only the chamber's yes/no totals, not the list's own tally or eligible membership.

techniques.evidence: features/volby/getListData.ts:52 Strict majority with tie→split is right. But there is no per-division line-support rule, an empty list gets 'split', not 'not measured', and the per-vote display omits the list's tally and eligible membership.
features/volby/getListData.ts:25 No pairwise agreement here. The surface lists 12 contested votes only.
